root:163 contract.algorithm_requirement.compute[4].math

For each (t,k,h), if route_ids[t,k] = -1 then Route[t,k,h] = bf16(0). Otherwise, with e = route_ids[t,k], Route[t,k,h] = bf16(sum_{j=0}^{I-1} QAct[t,k,j]*W2[e,h,j]). Each FC2 contraction uses independent FP32 accumulation before this BF16 RNE materialization. Routing weights are applied after it: Y[t,h] = bf16(sum_{k=0}^{K-1} Route[t,k,h]*route_weights[t,k]), with the products and route sum in FP32. A token with no valid routes produces zero. The no-bias zero-input case also produces zero. Overwrite all T*H elements of output and return [output], preserving its storage identity. Do not modify other inputs or storage outside this logical view; the generator's 64-element guards on each side are outside the write region. There is no caller-visible scratch. For the TP2 and TP8 geometries this is a local partial expert output; any cross-TP sum is performed by the caller outside this callable.

## t_15d7a5d9ab9672b0 | algorithm_contract.math | 1059 chars | 1 declarations

root:105 contract.algorithm_requirement.compute[1].math

For nibble c in {0,...,15}, F(c) has sign bit floor(c/8) and magnitude [0,0.5,1,1.5,2,3,4,FP4Max][c mod 8], preserving signed zero. For any row of L channels, with L divisible by Block, define Decode(q,s)[j] = F(floor(q[floor(j/2)] / 2^(4*(j mod 2))) mod 16) * s[floor(j/Block)], for 0 <= j < L. This rule applies independently to all preceding axes. For a prepared scale slice S with visible shape [N,C], Unswizzle(S) flattens S in row-major order, reshapes to [N/128,C/4,32,4,4], transposes axes to [0,3,2,1,4], and reshapes to [N,C]. Here N is divisible by 128 and C by 4 in every declared geometry. Define P(r) = 32*floor(r/32) + 8*(r mod 4) + floor((r mod 32)/4), and g(r) = 2*r for r < I, otherwise 2*(r-I)+1. A[t,:] = Decode(hidden_states[t,:], hidden_states_scale[t,:]). W1[e,r,:] = Decode(gemm1_weights[e,P(g(r)),:], Unswizzle(gemm1_weights_scale[e,:,:])[P(g(r)),:]), for 0 <= r < 2*I. W2[e,h,:] = Decode(gemm2_weights[e,P(h),:], Unswizzle(gemm2_weights_scale[e,:,:])[P(h),:]). All expert, token and hidden indices range over E, T and H respectively.

## t_2e940b8420f745e3 | algorithm_contract.math | 620 chars | 1 declarations

root:133 contract.algorithm_requirement.compute[2].math

For 0 <= t < T, 0 <= k < K and 0 <= j < I, let e = route_ids[t,k]. If e = -1, Act[t,k,j] = 0 without evaluating the expert expressions. Otherwise let u = sum_{h=0}^{H-1} A[t,h]*W1[e,j,h] and v = sum_{h=0}^{H-1} A[t,h]*W1[e,I+j,h]. If gemm1_clamp_limit is not None, let l = gemm1_clamp_limit[e] and replace u by clamp(u,-l,l) and v by min(v,l). Let alpha = gemm1_alpha[e], beta = gemm1_beta[e], and sigmoid(x) = 1/(1+exp(-x)); tanh is the hyperbolic tangent. Then Act[t,k,j] = v*sigmoid(alpha*v)*(u+beta) for activation_type = 3; Act[t,k,j] = alpha*tanh(v/alpha)*sigmoid(v) * (beta*tanh(u/beta)) for activation_type = 10.

## t_5013609e6f883052 | algorithm_contract.math | 662 chars | 1 declarations

root:148 contract.algorithm_requirement.compute[3].math

Independently for each (t,k) and 0 <= b < I/Block, let peak = max_{j=0}^{Block-1} abs(Act[t,k,b*Block+j]) and s = fp8_e4m3fn(clamp(peak*(1/FP4Max),0,ScaleMax)). The following per-channel formulas apply for 0 <= j < Block. If s = 0, QAct[t,k,b*Block+j] = 0 for the entire block. Otherwise let x = Act[t,k,b*Block+j]/s. Choose the nearest magnitude from the nonnegative values of F, saturating at FP4Max; a midpoint chooses the even magnitude-code index in {0,...,7}. Copy x's sign bit to the selected magnitude, yielding q, and set QAct[t,k,b*Block+j] = q*s. The scale conversion also uses RNE. This quantization uses no positive minimum scale and norm_const = 1.

## t_c98beb9f77d61637 | algorithm_contract.math | 1638 chars | 1 declarations

root:79 contract.algorithm_requirement.compute[0].math

None denotes Python None. The declared generated-call domain has 1 <= T <= TokenLimit, K = 8 and (H,I,E) in {(2048,768,128), (4096,768,128), (4096,1536,128), (7168,256,256)}. These geometries correspond respectively to Qwen3-30B TP1, Qwen3-235B TP2, Qwen3-235B TP1 and DeepSeek-V3 TP8. The ten fixed cases are samples, not the whole domain. H and I are divisible by Block; H and 2*I are divisible by 128, so the packed shapes and prepared scale tiles below have no padding. All tensors use their stated contiguous storage on the same CUDA device. topk_ids is the pair (route_ids, route_weights). Valid expert IDs are distinct within a token. Weights are softmax-normalized over the selected top-k logits before invalid routes are zeroed, without renormalization. Thus route_ids[t,k] = -1 implies route_weights[t,k] = 0, and each token's weight sum is at most 1 (up to FP32 rounding). Balanced, skewed, hotspot, masked and entirely empty routing, and zero activation payloads, are included. For activation_type = 3, gemm1_alpha is in [0.5,2] and gemm1_beta in [0,1], with defaults 1 and 0 when their generator options are omitted. For type 10, gemm1_alpha = 4 and gemm1_beta = 25 regardless of those generator options. Each of these tensors and any non-None clamp limit is uniform across experts in generated calls. The clamp may be None for either activation type. All other fixed arguments have the values stated in input; unspecified optional API modes outside this generated boundary are not included. Floating arithmetic and accumulation are FP32 with TF32 disabled, except for the explicit storage and quantization conversions below.

## t_38c0058da8c563a5 | dispatch.md | 307 chars | 1 declarations

dispatch.md:184 dispatch.md

每次实际 run_pipeline 的计算调用顺序由默认分支确定：cfg92 只有 direct；cfg97 是路由准备、flat gather、融合 FC1、FC2、finalize；cfg99 是小路由准备、split-K FC1、独立 activation/量化合并、FC2、finalize。大路由准备分别提交 count、scan、scatter，小路由准备只有 k_prepare_small；zflag 非空时在这些主干之前另提交一次 k_zero_verify。失败时保留该次实际接受的全部前缀，不撤销已经排队的工作，也不将未调用的后继计入提交。查表/scan 等 ABI 建立前缀仍属于同一请求。

## t_4b18cedfb080504b | dispatch.md | 271 chars | 1 declarations

dispatch.md:162 dispatch.md

小路由准备指 R=T*K 不超过 ABI 保存的 small_thresh，大路由准备指超过。默认建立 ABI 时，3000<R≤6500 且路由直方图非空取 3000，其余取 6500。FC1 默认在 R≤1536 选 cfg=99，否则选 cfg97；满足 MEGA 门且建立时直方图为空则改选 cfg92。FC2 的 WS 门比较路由 tile 数乘 (H/128)*max(1,I/256) 与 3072：仅上下界跨门限时读取直方图；WS 分支按 R≥32 选 81，否则 57，非 WS 分支在 I=256 选 23，否则选 44。

## t_5cf71081e9d2170d | dispatch.md | 243 chars | 1 declarations

例如 T=1、K=8、H=2048、I=768、E=128 的非空新请求选择 cfg/cfg2=99/44。zero_ok=false 时，scan 已提交对应 probe_split_mono，未提交对应 no_scan_split_mono；zero_ok=true 时对应 probe_verify_split_mono，查表发生时使用各自的 init 条目。它们只描述正常返回且主体完整提交的情况；终止错误及其实际前缀见覆盖缺口。各条件均在共享 Contract 全域独立求值。

线程处理宽度、网格数量、实际专家 tile 数、空工作、完整/部分 quadrant 和合法的 hoist 门保留参数化。cfg23 描述符拒绝后先改为 cfg12；相同 key 的拒绝被缓存，最终与 cfg44 的拒绝分支汇合到相同的 wide cp.async FC2，故不按来源 cfg 再复制回退节点。split_ws 的微小 R 分支只可能在本契约的 H=4096、I=1536 几何达到 WS 门；它和 split_mono 均达不到 ZERO2 的 T*H 门，不派生联合验证节点。

“普通复用”指 Model.forward 的 identity/key 缓存或默认 C 包装复用已发布 ABI，moe_run 返回零，且主干计算均已实际接受提交，只执行一次 run_pipeline 主体：可以是 eager、成功录图后的首次回放或已有完整图回放；不额外执行独立验证图，也没有私有流上的未捕获流水线提交。“联合复用”同样复用 ABI，但实际执行独立验证图和完整图各一次，且无私有流上的未捕获流水线提交。纯录图不产生这些计算的完成事件；外层图中的请求以真正回放为计算执行实例。

## t_92c9e52c42f438cc | dispatch.md | 462 chars | 1 declarations

dispatch.md:186 dispatch.md

具体退出边界：小准备属性设置失败返回 91/92；准备 launch 返回 31，大路由 memset 错误直接返回其代码，count/scan/scatter 的 launch 错误分别返回 32/33/34；flat gather 的 launch 错误返回 43；FC1 入口错误返回 100+gerr，此后不调用 activation、FC2 或 finalize；split-K activation 的 launch 错误返回 35；FC2 入口错误返回 200+gerr，此后不调用 finalize；finalize 的 launch 错误返回 36。最后的 cudaGetLastError 也可能在整条调用链已提交后才返回非零，不能将该情况倒推成零提交。cfg23 的 flat launch 未检查 launch_pdl 返回值，只查询 cudaGetLastError；因此返回零本身也不能替代每次提交已被接受的事实。发生错误的那次 launch 是否已接受按实际结果记录，不用错误码自行删除其工作。

## t_9630f3f8a4b67ff7 | dispatch.md | 280 chars | 1 declarations

dispatch.md:190 dispatch.md

BeginCapture 失败后源码仍调用私有非阻塞流上的 run_pipeline；随后还调用 caller-stream run_pipeline。此类请求包含两组实际接受的前缀，分别按上一段的阶段顺序和各自退出边界计数，不能把它们算成两次独立逻辑调用，也不能把第一组当作录图而抹去。两组使用同一个 Params：counts/fill、路由表、activation、rout 和 output 均共用地址；源码没有建立隔离这两组工作所需的跨流等待。即使第二组返回零，也不据此保证共享状态未被干扰或输出正确。这是已知实现缺陷范围，完整设计节点不覆盖该保证。

## t_bed08ee4398a6d3b | dispatch.md | 328 chars | 1 declarations

dispatch.md:176 dispatch.md

ABI 建立时，ensure_tables 按每设备标志决定是否提交 k_init_tables 并同步；非 direct 默认家族还调用 moe_zero_probe，其 malloc、memset、scan、同步和读回有不同错误出口。新 workspace 的清零依实际缓存命中情况发生，ABI 重建本身不等于所有初始化都发生。这些实际执行前缀属于同一次算子请求。probe 的负返回值使 Python 的 zero_ok 为 false，不由这一步直接终止 forward；后续不建立 zflag，不能把探测失败统一视为算子错误出口。probe 的 D2H cudaMemcpy 返回码未检查，返回判定只读取初值为 1 的 h，不能补造读回成功保证。

Host choices, scalar parameters and tensor bindings stay fixed at recording, while device tensor reads use the contents at execution. One thread per CTA handles the persistent int32[4] device state: word 0 holds FirstClean, word 1 the dirty aggregate, word 2 the arrival count; word 3 is unused and unchanged. If FirstPartDirty is nonzero, atomically OR 1 into word 1. Publish this contribution before atomically incrementing word 2 once. The final ticket observes all preceding contributions, writes FirstClean into word 0 and resets words 1 and 2 to zero. It then establishes system visibility and stores FirstMirror in the pinned mirror. Nonfinal ticket owners return without waiting for other CTAs. Done is this CTA's protocol completion, not an early grid-ready event. probe.kernel_done covers every output store and verdict; the mirror store alone does not certify full output completion. Words 1 and 2 begin at zero from ABI creation or the prior final ticket. probe.kernel_done precedes verify's output and protocol writes, so no first-pass store or atomic remains in flight when the full graph replaces the first versions. The host observation only selects submission; it does not replace this completion edge.

Initialize each thread's LocalBad to zero. Cooperatively evaluate all assigned zero_probe tests: four payload bytes per word, bytewise activation scales, scalar scores and expert parameters, then four scale bytes per word for each weight tensor. Keep each thread's rejection state across all these loops; do not exit after detecting a bad value. Skip limit accesses when the input is None. A CTA-wide OR rendezvous forms ProbeBad; one thread contributes 1 to global ProbeDirty for a bad bucket, and a clean bucket performs no global store. Buckets with no data still execute the rendezvous and this action's events. Done consumes LocalBad and covers any store submission; scan.kernel_done supplies external visibility. The global word's initialization, host consumption and cleanup are the service boundary specified by work_schedule, not a CTA-local reset.

FormatTables denotes the joint output E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and E4M3Pair. The CTA evaluates all byte codes and directly stores their entries in the module-global arrays defined by tables. No input staging or inter-thread exchange is needed. Kernel completion and the following device synchronization provide visibility; no table operand is passed to the later phases.

The elected thread atomically contributes a dirty bit if DirtyPart is nonzero, orders that contribution before taking one global arrival ticket, and then takes the ticket. The last arriving CTA observes the combined dirty state, writes Clean, and resets both counters for reuse. It also performs the optional pinned-mirror publication defined by verify. Other CTAs complete after their own contributions, without waiting for the last arrival. Done covers this CTA's state updates, not other CTAs' output stores; only verify.kernel_done exposes Clean and ZeroOutput to later grids. Counter reuse requires the previous execution and all its flag readers to have completed through the existing stream ordering.

Each warp owns its hardware TMEM quadrant (warp index modulo four), one row per lane. For c=0 or 1, load the matching 32 up and 32 gate values into this quadrant's rows of Fragment, issue both reads before waiting, and wait for all their TMEM reads to retire. Done makes this register fragment usable.

One elected lane atomically ORs a dirty contribution when nonzero, orders it before its arrival increment with device visibility, and obtains one unique arrival ticket. The other lanes perform no atomic publication, but remain part of this action. Host observation of MirrorFirst is not a device completion event.

Read PackedExpert's backing row and reject out-of-range IDs before any per-expert parameter access. Accepted groups merge the retained slices into Merged in ascending order, then compute merge_quantize into Activated. Four-lane maximum exchange combines all 16 absolute values; paired neighbor exchange assembles packed payload words. Store ActQ and one ActS byte per accepted block, including unused backing rows that pass the check. No cross-block or cross-CTA exchange is needed. Rejected groups perform no arithmetic or stores, but the action still completes. PartialLoad is dead after the merge; Merged is dead after activation; Activated is dead after quantization and store submission.

This protocol does not spin or require all CTAs to be resident together. Kernel completion covers every zero store and state update; downstream guards wait for that full completion. Stage every route ID once into StagedIds and zero the full GroupTable, including the unused expert columns. After CTA rendezvous, warp g forms Hist(g) for its contiguous route group. Rendezvous before expert-wise prefixing replaces Hist with RankCursor, the group-exclusive reservation bases of routing, and writes Counts. Another rendezvous precedes the paired expert scans; ScanScratch holds two 64-word scan arrays and J. Publish Offs and TilePrefix both globally and into their local caches, then rendezvous before scatter and tile enumeration. Each warp advances its own RankCursor by atomics while writing RoutePos and all three packed maps. Enumerate and store TileExpert and TileRow from the cached tile prefix. StagedIds and the prefix caches survive through their last reads; GroupTable is overwritten only after histogram production is complete. M=0 still writes zero Counts/prefixes and RoutePos=-1, with no packed or tile stores.

On Clean=1 this action is a no-op with no payload or scratch access. Otherwise: Read PackedExpert's backing row and reject out-of-range IDs before any per-expert parameter access. Accepted groups merge the retained slices into Merged in ascending order, then compute merge_quantize into Activated. Four-lane maximum exchange combines all 16 absolute values; paired neighbor exchange assembles packed payload words. Store ActQ and one ActS byte per accepted block, including unused backing rows that pass the check. No cross-block or cross-CTA exchange is needed. Rejected groups perform no arithmetic or stores, but the action still completes. PartialLoad is dead after the merge; Merged is dead after activation; Activated is dead after quantization and store submission.

Reduce LocalDirty to DirtyPart with a CTA-wide OR. Use the same four-int32 global state as first_verify, whose dirty accumulator and arrival counter are now reset. A dirty CTA leader atomically ORs the dirty word with one; every leader executes a device release fence and atomically increments the arrival counter once. The last ticket holder reads the combined dirty word, publishes Clean, resets dirty and arrival words, and performs a system fence before overwriting the pinned mirror with HostVerdict. Non-last CTAs do not spin or require grid-wide residency. This publication does not imply completion of other CTAs' zero stores: verify.kernel_done supplies full-grid visibility for the output and device verdict. Guards consume this second Clean only. No host observation is required after this grid. State and mirror remain allocated with the ABI; same-stream ordering completes this grid and all guard readers before another request may overwrite them.

Each thread initializes its DirtyAccumulator word to zero, submits its strided 16-byte FirstZeroY stores, and accumulates dirty bits over its assigned payload words, scale bytes, scores and parameters. Done covers the vote and zero-store submission; it does not claim global output completion.

FormatTables denotes FormatPair, FormatScale and FormatScalePair together. The eight warps partition the 256 byte codes, evaluate format_tables and write every entry to its device-global module array. No invocation tensor, shared staging buffer or cross-thread exchange is needed. Done covers computation and store submission; kernel_done makes the table writes visible before the host device synchronization returns. The arrays remain allocated after this role exits.

Initialize one unsigned predicate accumulator per participating thread in ScanAccum. Cooperatively read and test this shard's assigned inputs, carrying each accumulator across all local loops without early exit. A CTA-wide any reduction and rendezvous produce ProbePart. The elected writer contributes 1 to global Dirty only for a nonzero part; a zero part submits no store. No member reads Dirty, and no CTA waits for another shard. Done covers the shard's reads, reduction and any store submission; kernel completion supplies visibility for host readback. Even a shard without tests completes the reduction with zero.

Initialize each thread's Dirty accumulator to zero. Each thread first submits 16-byte zero stores for its flattened output words, without reading old output, then traverses payload words, scale bytes, scores and expert parameters in separate grid-stride loops, OR-ing verification's predicates. Test the clamp only when supplied. There is no CTA barrier between these loops. A final CTA-wide OR and rendezvous forms BlockDirty after all threads have submitted output stores and completed their checks. Done does not imply global completion of the output stores.

verify_split_ws:625 design.tile_pipeline.phase.prepare.role.Main.info.verb.produce

On Active=0 this declared action is a no-op with issue/done and no data access or store. On Active=1: Stage every route ID once into StagedIds and zero the full GroupTable, including the unused expert columns. After CTA rendezvous, warp g forms Hist(g) for its contiguous route group. Rendezvous before expert-wise prefixing replaces Hist with RankCursor, the group-exclusive reservation bases of routing, and writes Counts. Another rendezvous precedes the paired expert scans; ScanScratch holds two 64-word scan arrays and J. Publish Offs and TilePrefix both globally and into their local caches, then rendezvous before scatter and tile enumeration. Each warp advances its own RankCursor by atomics while writing RoutePos and all three packed maps. Enumerate and store TileExpert and TileRow from the cached tile prefix. StagedIds and the prefix caches survive through their last reads; GroupTable is overwritten only after histogram production is complete. M=0 still writes zero Counts/prefixes and RoutePos=-1, with no packed or tile stores.

First execute the guard's predecessor-grid wait and read Clean. For Clean=1, read no metadata and allocate no TensorStorage; work domains are empty and grid completion supplies launch_ready without an explicit trigger. For Clean=0, repeat the predecessor wait and let warp 0 trigger dependent launches, then read J. J=0 leaves the work domains empty without allocating TensorStorage. Otherwise initialize the shared completion protocol, allocate TensorStorage from warp 0 and rendezvous the CTA, including workers with no assigned item.

Initialize each thread's ProbeFlags word to zero. Each thread accumulates its assigned predicates through the five scan passes, retaining its word between passes. Payload loads examine four bytes together and ignore each nibble's sign bit; weight-scale loads examine four encoded scales together. Threads whose local ranges are empty retain zero. A CTA-wide Boolean OR and rendezvous form ProbePart; only the designated leader publishes 1 to global ProbeDirty when the partial is nonzero. There is no cross-CTA rendezvous or PDL entry. Done consumes the local flags and submits any verdict store; kernel completion supplies visibility for host inspection. A zero partial still completes this action but does not write the flag.

Process the two 32-column chunks in order. A quadrant whose entire 32-row group is valid converts to BF16 and uses its own Sink region: wait until all earlier bulk stores by that warp have finished reading Sink, rendezvous the warp, populate Sink, establish async-proxy visibility, rendezvous, and issue/commit the bulk store. Repeat for the second chunk, reusing that same region. A partial quadrant converts and directly stores only valid rows and never writes Sink. Done covers conversion, Fragment consumption and store submission; it is not a global-completion event. The bulk read wait also protects Sink across worktiles, even when intervening quadrants used direct stores.

Thread 0 atomically ORs the shared global dirty word when Check is nonzero, establishes device visibility, and atomically increments the arrival word. The last ticket holder reads the accumulated dirty word, writes Clean, then resets both reduction words for the next verification. Establish system visibility before overwriting the pinned word with HostVerdict; no host poll follows it. Other ticket holders do not publish the final verdict. This protocol does not spin or require all CTAs to be resident together. Kernel completion covers every zero store and state update; downstream guards wait for that full completion. ZeroState remains available to downstream guards; same-stream kernel order protects its next device use. HostVerdict has no downstream device consumer here; a later graph_replay may reset the pinned word from the host without waiting for this request to complete. Publication consumes FirstState's reset reduction words under the graph-boundary dependency, without reading FirstClean or FirstZeroY.

On Active=0 this declared action is a no-op with issue/done and no data access or store. On Active=1: Read PackedExpert's backing row and reject out-of-range IDs before any per-expert parameter access. Accepted groups merge the retained slices into Merged in ascending order, then compute merge_quantize into Activated. Four-lane maximum exchange combines all 16 absolute values; paired neighbor exchange assembles packed payload words. Store ActQ and one ActS byte per accepted block, including unused backing rows that pass the check. No cross-block or cross-CTA exchange is needed. Rejected groups perform no arithmetic or stores, but the action still completes. PartialLoad is dead after the merge; Merged is dead after activation; Activated is dead after quantization and store submission.

Initialize one unsigned rejection state per thread. Threads stride through the shard's token-row payload words and scale bytes, then its routing weights, expert parameters and both prepared scale arrays. Payload words retain only the eight E2M1 magnitude fields; packed scale words test all four bytes. Optional clamp loads occur only when HasLimit=1. Accumulate every predicate locally without an early exit. All 256 threads participate in the CTA-wide OR, including threads with no assigned elements. One thread sets ProbeDirty to 1 if this OR rejects; otherwise no global store occurs. No CTA polls the word or waits for another CTA. Completion includes this local scan and conditional store; kernel completion supplies host-visible readiness. The fixed source uses non-atomic shared-flag stores, so this design records the monotone publication without asserting race-free execution.

Dirty OR and arrivals start at zero from ABI construction or the preceding completed verification. Reduce DirtyVote with a CTA-wide Boolean OR. A dirty member atomically ORs one into the retained global dirty word. Its elected thread makes that update visible before taking one atomic arrival ticket; clean members also take a ticket. The last member reads the aggregate, stores ZeroClean and resets dirty and arrivals to zero. Nonlast members finish after their arrival; last-member completion includes verdict publication and reset. One thread per CTA handles the persistent int32[4] device state: word 0 holds FirstClean, word 1 the dirty aggregate, word 2 the arrival count; word 3 is unused and unchanged. If FirstPartDirty is nonzero, atomically OR 1 into word 1. Publish this contribution before atomically incrementing word 2 once. The final ticket observes all preceding contributions, writes FirstClean into word 0 and resets words 1 and 2 to zero. It then establishes system visibility and stores FirstMirror in the pinned mirror. Nonfinal ticket owners return without waiting for other CTAs. Done is this CTA's protocol completion, not an early grid-ready event. probe.kernel_done covers every output store and verdict; the mirror store alone does not certify full output completion. Words 1 and 2 begin at zero from this ABI creation. probe.kernel_done precedes verify's output and protocol writes, so no first-pass store or atomic remains in flight when the full graph replaces the first versions. The host observation only selects submission; it does not replace this completion edge.

Consume PayloadA/PayloadB and ScaleTM in four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates to C1. The first update initializes C1 without reading its old value. The fused 128-column product covers both up and gate. Issue a cumulative completion commit after each stage; done covers scale copies, payload reads and accumulator updates. The last stage also commits result readiness for the epilogue. Same-issuer ordering ensures an earlier MMA has consumed ScaleTM before a later scale copy overwrites that scale slot, and makes each scale copy visible before the MMA that uses it.

First wait for predecessor-grid completion and read Clean. Clean=1 completes this entry without an explicit launch trigger, J read or local allocation; launch_ready is then supplied by kernel completion. Otherwise execute the PDL wait/trigger pair before reading J. For J=0 there is no local allocation and work domains are empty. For J>0 initialize completion state and allocate TensorStorage via warp 0, then rendezvous all four warps, including idle workers. Ring position and completion parity start once per worker and continue across its worktiles.

Resolve successive assigned worktiles using a stepped row-tile/column cursor equivalent to work_schedule's strided sequence. A descriptor contains the selected expert, compact row base, valid row bound and output-column origin; ordinary per-lane address encodings do not change these coordinates. Initial descriptors go to Metadata's three-slot ring. Later descriptors go to the single Pending register set, without overwriting the still-live ring entry. Metadata remains needed through that worktile's payload issue, scale fetch and output store submission.

No PDL entry or launch-ready signal belongs to this scan.

After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

## t_ede528aa8a6489e6 | pipeline.verb | 477 chars | 1 declarations

init_probe_fused_big_flat:648 design.tile_pipeline.phase.tables.role.Main.info.verb.produce

FormatTables denotes E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and E4M3Pair from format_tables. Each of the 256 threads computes the entries for its byte value, rounds the three BF16 values and stores the low/high pair, FP32 scale and duplicated BF16 scale pair in their global arrays. No thread reads another thread's entries; no CTA barrier, shared tile or local reuse protocol is needed. Done includes computation and store submission; kernel completion establishes the tables' global visibility.

## t_eec4b1918be671b1 | pipeline.verb | 418 chars | 1 declarations

init_probe_verify_fused_serial:692 design.tile_pipeline.phase.init.role.Main.info.verb.produce

TableEntries comprises PairTable, ScaleTable and ScalePairTable. Each thread evaluates init_tables for one distinct byte code and writes its three device-global entries. Intermediate conversions are local temporaries; there is no shared buffer, barrier or lookup-table read. Done covers this role's store submissions; init.kernel_done and the following device synchronization establish completion of every table write.

For Clean=1 this action is a no-op with issue/done events: it neither reads routing data nor writes Y. Otherwise each thread owns FinalWidth independent output elements. Hoist its eight route indices and scores, initialize Accumulator, then consume valid BF16 route vectors in increasing slot order using finalize's FMA recurrence. Convert and store Y once; no CTA reduction or inter-thread barrier is required. Empty routing still writes zeros.

PrefixScratch holds 257 tile-prefix entries, two 64-word scan arrays and the tile total. Warp-local scans, the scan of warp totals and CTA rendezvous produce both prefixes. Rendezvous all eight warps with a CTA-wide Boolean OR of DirtyLane, producing DirtyPart. One thread per CTA atomically ORs a dirty contribution into the global sticky aggregate when needed, establishes device visibility, then obtains an arrival ticket. Only the final arrival reads the aggregate, publishes Clean and resets aggregate and ticket to zero. Other CTAs perform no publication of Clean and do not wait for the last CTA. The pinned host mirror is absent in this node. This action completes after this CTA's contribution and any elected publication/reset; verify.kernel_done covers all contributions, output stores and the verdict. DirtyLane is dead after the reduction; the global protocol state is reused only after the ordered execution completes.
